req.title: Reject wrong method on /patch
req.statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 405 for methods other than PATCH on /patch.

doc.reasoning: The requirement states that /patch must accept PATCH and reject all other HTTP methods with 405. I design: (1) a positive test confirming PATCH returns 200 with expected JSON payload keys, (2) negative tests for GET, POST, PUT, DELETE each expecting exactly 405, (3) a boundary/decision-table test covering the full set of disallowed methods systematically. Each test uses exact status code assertions to catch comparison-operator mutations, and the positive test asserts payload structure to catch return-value mutations.

from httpbin.core import app

def test_patch_method_returns_200_with_payload():
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.patch('/patch')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    data = r.get_json()
    assert isinstance(data, dict)
    for key in ('url', 'args', 'form', 'data', 'origin', 'headers', 'files', 'json'):
        assert key in data

test_patch_method_returns_200_with_payload()

tests.name: test_all_disallowed_methods_on_patch_return_exactly_405
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
actions: Send GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, HEAD requests to /patch
Assert each returns exactly 405 and not 200, 404, or 500
expected: All disallowed methods return exactly HTTP 405
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app

def test_all_disallowed_methods_on_patch_return_exactly_405():
    client = app.test_client()
    disallowed = [
        client.get('/patch'),
        client.post('/patch'),
        client.put('/patch'),
        client.delete('/patch'),
    ]
    for r in disallowed:
        assert r.status_code == 405
        assert r.status_code != 200
        assert r.status_code != 404
        assert r.status_code != 500
    allowed = client.patch('/patch')
    assert allowed.status_code == 200
    assert allowed.status_code != 405

test_all_disallowed_methods_on_patch_return_exactly_405()

tests.name: test_patch_response_payload_exact_keys_and_not_405
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
actions: Send PATCH request to /patch with JSON body
Assert response JSON contains exactly the expected top-level keys
expected: JSON payload has keys: url, args, form, data, origin, headers, files, json
trace: view_patch calls get_dict with url, args, form, data, origin, headers, files, json
BVA: status code boundary between 200 (allowed) and 405 (disallowed)
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
import json as _json

def test_patch_response_payload_exact_keys_and_not_405():
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.patch(
        '/patch',
        data=_json.dumps({'key': 'value'}),
        content_type='application/json'
    )
    assert r.status_code == 200
    assert r.status_code != 405
    assert r.status_code != 201
    body = r.get_json()
    expected_keys = {'url', 'args', 'form', 'data', 'origin', 'headers', 'files', 'json'}
    assert set(body.keys()) == expected_keys
    assert body['json'] == {'key': 'value'}

test_patch_response_payload_exact_keys_and_not_405()
